lines.en: Dario, you look upset. What happened at work today? You’ve barely touched your coffee.
lines.pt: Dario, você parece chateada. O que aconteceu no trabalho hoje? Você mal tocou no café.

lines.en: I lost my temper with a client this morning. If I were more patient, I would listen better.
lines.pt: Perdi a paciência com um cliente hoje de manhã. Se eu fosse mais paciente, ouviria melhor.

lines.en: Oh no. What did he say? Clients can be really difficult sometimes, but we all have bad days.
lines.pt: Ai, não. O que ele disse? Clientes às vezes são muito difíceis, mas todos temos dias ruins.

lines.en: He kept interrupting me and asking for a discount, and I snapped. I said something I shouldn’t have.
lines.pt: Ele ficava me interrompendo e pedindo desconto, e eu explodi. Disse algo que não devia.

lines.en: Wow. Well, if I were you, I would call him and say sorry before the end of the week.
lines.pt: Nossa. Bem, se eu fosse você, ligaria para ele e pediria desculpas antes do fim da semana.

lines.en: You’re right, but I’m embarrassed. You’re so organized all the time.
lines.pt: Você tem razão, mas estou envergonhada. Você é tão organizado o tempo todo.

lines.en: Ha! Not really. I just hide it well. I get nervous before every meeting, and my hands shake.
lines.pt: Ha! Nem tanto. Eu só escondo bem. Fico nervoso antes de toda reunião, e as minhas mãos tremem.

lines.en: Seriously? I had no idea. Maybe I’m too hard on myself. Everybody gets stressed, right?
lines.pt: Sério? Não fazia ideia. Talvez eu seja dura demais comigo mesma. Todo mundo fica estressado, não é?

lines.en: Absolutely. And if you had more confidence, you wouldn’t worry so much about one bad call.
lines.pt: Com certeza. E se você tivesse mais confiança, não se preocuparia tanto com uma única ligação ruim.

lines.en: That’s a good point. I’ll write him an email tonight, and I’ll keep it short and honest.
lines.pt: Boa observação. Vou escrever um e-mail para ele hoje à noite, curto e sincero.

lines.en: Great plan. I’ll buy the dessert.
lines.pt: Ótimo plano. Eu pago a sobremesa.

facts.big: If I were more patient, I would listen better
facts.label: Segundo condicional
facts.sub: Use If + passado, would + verbo para situações imaginárias. Para conselho: If I were you, I would….

facts.label: se eu fosse
facts.sub: Use If I were para imaginar uma qualidade que você não tem agora: If I were more patient. Com I, he e she, em conselhos use were.

facts.label: eu faria
facts.sub: Depois da condição use would + verbo sem to: I would listen better. A forma curta é I’d: I’d listen better.

compare.ask: If I were more patient, I would listen better.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “se eu fosse mais paciente, escutaria melhor”.
compare.tip: Diga: “if I were more patient, I would listen better.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use If + passado + would + verbo: If I were more patient, I would listen better. Com be, use were para todas as pessoas. Para conselho, use If I were you, I would….

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: If I were more patient, I would listen better.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: If I were more patient is not real now.
We say “If I was you” only in formal English.
items.why: If I were you is the usual advice form, but was is also used in speech.

items.s: After would we use the base verb.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: If I were more patient is not real now. → Verdadeiro (Yes, it is imaginary.)
We say “If I was you” only in formal English. → Falso (If I were you is the usual advice form, but was is also used in speec…)
After would we use the base verb. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A home in Leeds · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Tuesday evening in Leeds. Fay opens the door and sees her friend Leo. His face looks tired and sad. She makes tea and brings two cups. Leo sits on the sofa with a long sigh. He starts to explain his bad day.

“Leo, you look upset. What happened at work today?” says Fay. “I lost my temper with a client. If I were more patient, I would listen better.” says Leo. “If I were you, I would call the client and say sorry.” says Fay.

pages.title: A home in Leeds · 3/3
paragraphs: “Maybe, but if I were calmer, I would be boring!” says Leo. “I don’t think so. If you were boring, I wouldn’t be your friend.” says Fay. Leo drinks his tea and feels calmer. He decides to write the client an email. Fay helps him choose the right words. They laugh about the bad day. Leo thanks Fay for her good advice. Wishing is easy, but changing takes practice.
